correctness.rationale: Verified polynomial cofactor identity Fdot=(lambda+eta z)zF symbolically with F=(x^2+y^2-a^2)^2+z^2-1. On a>1 smooth torus use r^2=a^2+cos phi, z=sin phi and theta=arg(x+iy); recover exact original-time equations phidot=-(a^2+cos phi)(lambda+eta sin phi)/2 and thetadot=-c(a^2+cos phi)sin(2theta)/2. For lambda>eta the negatively oriented longitudinal circuit is strictly monotone, giving exactly four fixed meridian angles and return tan(theta_next)=exp(-4pi c/sqrt(lambda^2-eta^2))tan(theta). The denominator partial fraction identity checked independently reduces T=2*integral dphi/[(a^2+cos phi)(lambda+eta sin phi)] to displayed closed form. The original-time period is minimal because phi winds once monotonically. Theta scalar monotonicity excludes off-meridian periodic motion. At lambda=eta each meridian has one stationary longitudinal phase plus a homoclinic arc; for lambda<eta stationary phases prevent any periodic orbit. Expanding T and log multiplier yields both sharp square-root scalings and distinct transverse exponents at lambda->eta and a->1. Relative torus stability only, not ambient normal Floquet multiplier. Script finite quadratures are corroborative.

value.rationale: Four-cycle configurations of cubic vector fields on algebraic tori are a natural dynamical system. Exact minimal physical periods, relative Floquet multipliers and two different square-root infinite-period mechanisms separate loss of longitudinal velocity from geometric torus pinching, a real structural distinction that qualitative orbit counts do not show. The two critical limits give reusable asymptotic boundary information, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
